1	# 《嘉宾》歌曲分析
2	
3	分析日期：2026-11-02（Asia/Taipei）。分析对象为本目录的 `嘉宾.m4a`，歌词底稿为 `嘉宾.lrc`，原始文件未修改。
4	
5	歌曲写一个已经分手的人参加前任婚礼：外界的喜庆逐渐压垮尚未结束的眷恋，叙述者经历克制、失控、离席和自省，最后开始接受关系边界、收回自己的生活。结尾仍有遗憾和祝愿，不能简单判作已经完全释怀。
6	
7	实测适用节奏约 **75 BPM**；主体段拟合为 **75.0109 BPM**。完整节拍表有 **399 个算法节拍点**。最后明显重音的声学候选为 **05:19.93–05:19.95**，之后 **05:25.985** 还有较弱起音；两者的区别和识别局限见下文。
8	
9	## 1. 文件与版本
10	
11	| 项目 | 结果 |
12	| --- | --- |
13	| 歌曲身份 | 张远《嘉宾》，普通话单曲版；依据本地元数据及发行曲库交叉核对 |
14	| 本地专辑标注 | 嘉宾 - Single |
15	| 发行日期 | 2020-10-26；文件创建日期不作为发行日期 |
16	| 音频 | AAC LC，44,100 Hz，立体声 |
17	| 原文件时长 | 333.676621 秒，即 05:33.677 |
18	| 分析解码时长 | 333.676644 秒；重采样产生约 0.000023 秒差异 |
19	| 歌词 | 46 行；首行 00:21.26，末行起点 05:04.82 |
20	
21	[LINE MUSIC 发行页](https://music-tw.line.me/album/7532028)与本地演唱者、发行日一致。[广州日报对张远的采访](https://huacheng.gz-cmc.com/pages/2021/01/17/2883c1eaf20f40249a71f12152d58486.html)也核实原唱身份。以上不能证明文件从未被编辑；本报告的时间全部以当前 M4A 为准。
22	
23	## 2. 网络解读与听众接收：四种常见理解
24	
25	检索使用 WebSearch，并通过网页正文及 Exa 抓取核对来源。这里的“主流理解”指这些可核实材料中常见的理解方向；没有对全平台评论抽样，不能据此宣称多数听众持有某一观点。发行宣传、媒体乐评和听众个人感受分开标明。
26	
27	### 2.1 从亲密关系退到旁观位置，婚礼让失去成为现实
28	
29	核心痛点是身份改变：曾经参与对方生活的人，如今只能见证另一个人的承诺。婚礼的公共喜悦放大了私人失落，副歌不断回到“嘉宾”身份，使关系结束的事实无法回避。
30	
31	贵州音乐广播的原文直接从前任婚礼、旁观者处境和心酸理解歌曲；豆瓣原始长评则把这种失去延伸到未曾正式开始的少年暗恋。前者更贴近本地歌词叙事，后者属于听众投射，不能据此改变歌曲人物已经分手的设定。来源：[贵州音乐广播，2023-10-18](https://www.gzstv.com/a/d71d3e43cc28464e810eb78ac924f799)、[豆瓣用户「。」原始乐评，2021-07-11](https://music.douban.com/review/13670549/)。
32	
33	### 2.2 体面祝福与内心疼痛并存，离席是承受极限
34	
35	感谢邀请、提醒自己不要逃避、礼貌寒暄，都可以读作努力维持体面。叙述者想祝福，又无法压下失落；离开现场给情绪留出空间。这一“自我保护”的判断来自本地歌词，不能进一步推断新娘故意伤害他。
36	
37	豆瓣长评写出难以平静祝福、又希望对方幸福的矛盾；听众作者东山南讨论原版从苦涩到祝福、退场的心境。这些个人评论支持歌曲的复杂感受，不能当作歌手本人经历。来源：[豆瓣原始乐评](https://music.douban.com/review/13670549/)、[东山南听众评论，2021-11-14](https://www.popdaily.com.tw/forum/entertainment/1164146)。
38	
39	### 2.3 告别带来清醒，逐步把自己还给自己
40	
41	婚礼既是失去的证据，也成为结束等待的契机。末段的重点逐渐由对方转向自身：承认无法继续参与对方的人生，开始恢复自己的主体性。最后仍祝愿对方得到更好的爱，因此这里的接受带有残余疼痛。
42	
43	LINE MUSIC 刊载的发行简介明确呈现崩溃、释然与清醒；贵州音乐广播将放手解释为成熟与尊重；东山南也把普通话原版结尾理解为面对自己。来源：[LINE MUSIC 发行简介](https://music-tw.line.me/album/7532028)、[贵州音乐广播](https://www.gzstv.com/a/d71d3e43cc28464e810eb78ac924f799)、[东山南原文](https://www.popdaily.com.tw/forum/entertainment/1164146)。其中发行简介属于宣传文案，不能充当独立听众意见。
44	
45	### 2.4 从错过反观当下：珍惜眼前，接受关系不可逆
46	
47	部分听众将歌曲听成对自身关系的提醒：尚能沟通时要珍惜，关系真正结束后就需要接受其边界。这是听众对歌曲的生活化延伸，歌曲没有交代分手原因，也没有给出挽回关系的方法。
48	
49	豆瓣原始短评中，DrZou（2020-11-14）由歌曲谈到相处与错过；mumu_L（2021-05-03）则把能成为嘉宾视为仍有缘分。后一种看法比歌曲表面的苦涩更温和，可视作同一题材的不同接收方式。来源：[豆瓣《嘉宾》原始短评页](https://music.douban.com/subject/35238236/comments/)。这一方向的直接样本较少，代表性低于前三项。
50	
51	## 3. 主题与情绪走向
52	
53	**主题：在旧爱的婚礼上承认亲密关系已结束，经历失去身份的疼痛，并开始完成自我告别。** “嘉宾”既指婚礼身份，也承载了只能短暂停留、无法再参与未来的关系位置。这是结合歌词及上述资料作出的文本解释。
54	
55	| 时间 | 叙事与情绪 | 与音乐测量的关系 |
56	| --- | --- | --- |
57	| 00:00.00–00:21.26 | 前奏，情绪尚未由歌词明确命名 | 前奏整体能量较低 |
58	| 00:21.26–00:46.86 | 偶尔回想，被突来的婚讯打断，错愕 | 第一主歌；情绪的突然变化主要依据歌词 |
59	| 00:46.86–01:35.82 | 别人开心、自己清醒；走进婚礼，努力克制并反复确认身份 | 预副歌与副歌；整体能量高于第一主歌 |
60	| 01:35.82–02:14.88 | 疏离的寒暄刺激旧伤；尾句后进入间奏，留下消化情绪的空间 | 约 01:51.97 出现音色结构转折，随后有明显低能量区 |
61	| 02:14.88–03:47.49 | 戒指、仪式和婚礼细节让痛感具体化；想祝福却承受不住，选择离席 | 第二主歌至副歌，平均能量整体高于第一轮 |
62	| 03:47.49–04:02.05 | 桥段审视自身投入，带自嘲与难堪 | 功能依据歌词位置与段落关系判读 |
63	| 04:02.05–04:50.46 | 承认无资格继续关心，仍难以祝福，随后转向清醒和自我收回 | 终副歌；情绪开始转向，能量并非逐句下降 |
64	| 04:50.46–05:10.20 | 放轻姿态，以带着遗憾的祝愿收束 | 平均 RMS 明显下降；区间包含末句后的留白 |
65	| 05:10.20–05:33.68 | 尾奏，余绪延长、逐渐消散 | 尾段起音与衰减；末尾低能量区见第 5 节 |
66	
67	这一走向允许克制与失控交替。无法仅凭音量断言人物的心理状态，也不能从歌词推出背叛、恶意炫耀或歌手的真实恋爱经历。
68	
69	## 4. librosa：BPM、节拍点与段落
70	
71	### 4.1 方法与 BPM
72	
73	ffmpeg 将当前音轨解码为单声道、22,050 Hz 浮点 PCM。使用 librosa **0.11.0**，`hop_length=512`，帧间隔约 **23.22 ms**；分别计算完整音轨的均值／中位数起音包络，以及 HPSS 打击声部的中位数包络，比较 `start_bpm=60/80/120`。
74	
75	`beat_track` 的原始估计主要为 **75.999540** 或 **151.999081 BPM**，均值包络在初值 60 时也得到 **73.828125 BPM**。这是离散时间分辨率、倍半速和起始先验共同影响的估计，不能把小数位当作实际精度。[librosa beat_track 官方说明](https://librosa.org/doc/0.11.0/generated/librosa.beat.beat_track.html)说明了其依据起音强度、相关性与动态规划选取节拍的过程。
76	
77	本文件的慢速直接跟踪在前半段较不稳定。完整音轨中位数包络的双速序列在 25–110 秒拟合约 150.1343 BPM，在 135–220 秒约 149.9825 BPM；据此每隔一个检测脉冲保留一次，得到约 75 BPM 的节拍序列。两种奇偶相位按 135–285 秒平均起音强度选择，本次选择相位 1；这不等于确认了小节首拍。
78	
79	| 拟合范围 | BPM | 相对该范围匀速拟合的时间残差 RMS |
80	| --- | ---: | ---: |
81	| 00:25–05:00，主体 | 75.0109 | 0.0417 秒 |
82	| 00:25–01:50 | 75.0648 | 0.0461 秒 |
83	| 02:15–03:40，稳定段 | 74.9902 | 0.0114 秒 |
84	| 04:02–05:00 | 75.0588 | 0.0599 秒 |
85	
86	**用于 MV 的节奏参考：75 BPM，约 0.800 秒一拍；更密的剪辑可参考约 150 BPM 的细分脉冲。** 不据此断言有 75→150 的变速。上述残差表示算法序列与匀速网格的贴合程度，未经乐谱或听辨校准，不能作为真实演奏误差。
87	
88	### 4.2 节拍点
89	
90	完整结果见 [节拍点.csv](/Users/oyamahappa/Documents/GitHub/Motion/嘉宾/节拍点.csv)，共 **399 点**。前 8 点（秒）：`1.973696, 2.763175, 3.552653, 4.342132, 5.131610, 5.897868, 6.640907, 7.430385`。最后一点为 **319.947755 秒（05:19.948）**。
91	
92	CSV 序号从 1 起，仅表示检测顺序。节拍点不等于小节首拍、重音或歌词起点；前奏和低能量处可靠性较低。319.948 秒之后仍有声音，算法没有继续输出节拍，不向尾奏硬补匀速网格。
93	
94	### 4.3 段落时间表
95	
96	时间从文件开头计，区间左闭右开。L01–L46 为原始 LRC 行号。带歌词的边界采用 LRC 起点；间奏起点采用 MFCC 分段转折候选；尾奏采用低能量空档后强起音候选。段落功能是结合重复歌词作出的分析，librosa 不会直接识别“主歌／副歌”。[MFCC 时间聚类所用接口](https://librosa.org/doc/0.11.0/generated/librosa.segment.agglomerative.html)只提供音色结构候选。

99	| --- | --- | --- | --- |

101	| 主歌一 | 00:21.260–00:46.860 | L01–L04，回忆与婚讯 | 00:20.944 |

115	| 尾奏 | 05:10.195–05:33.677 | 310.195 秒强起音与随后衰减；MFCC 另有 310.497 秒转折，边界中等置信 | 05:10.544 |

117	歌词起点和最近节拍有时相差约 0.3 秒，可能涉及弱起、演唱延迟或 LRC 误差。本报告保留两套时间，不自动挪动字幕。间奏与尾奏的边界尚未逐句听辨，不宜直接当作精确的人声结束时刻。

119	## 5. 停顿与最后一个重音
120	
121	### 5.1 可复核的低能量停顿
122	
123	以 2,048 采样窗口计算 RMS，再取 13 帧移动平均（约 0.302 秒）；相对全曲未平滑 RMS 峰值，连续低于 **−40 dB** 且持续至少 **0.35 秒**，标作明显低能量区。它可能含残响或很轻的伴奏，不等于数字静音，也不能证明没有人声。
124	
125	| 时间 | 持续 | 位置解释 |
126	| --- | ---: | --- |
127	| 00:00.000–00:00.929 | 0.929 秒 | 文件开头低能量 |
128	| 01:55.566–01:56.796 | 1.231 秒 | 间奏前部明显留白候选 |
129	| 05:08.709–05:09.986 | 1.277 秒 | 末句之后、尾奏强起音之前的留白候选 |
130	| 05:18.973–05:19.344 | 0.372 秒 | 尾奏中的短空档 |
131	| 05:29.166–05:33.677 | 4.511 秒 | 末尾衰减至低能量 |
132	
133	较宽松的 **−32 dB** 阈值还检出 01:54.683–01:56.866、01:59.583–02:01.394 等较长低能量区；阈值全部结果保存在 JSON。−50 dB 下末尾低能量从 **05:31.465** 开始。前奏、间奏和句间间隔与上述能量停顿分别记录，不把整段无人演唱的区间称作静音。
134	
135	### 5.2 最后明显重音与较弱收尾起音
136	
137	操作性定义：在 280 秒以后寻找起音峰，峰间隔至少 0.15 秒、突出度至少为全曲起音包络 P70；再要求强度达到全曲 **P95**、相对 RMS 高于 −35 dB，并且起音前后短窗口能量增加至少 **3 dB**。这一判据识别声学重音候选，不能取代音乐听辨。[librosa 起音检测说明](https://librosa.org/doc/0.11.0/generated/librosa.onset.onset_detect.html)区分了起音包络峰与具体音乐解释。
138	
139	| 判断 | 时间 | 依据与置信范围 |
140	| --- | --- | --- |
141	| **最后明显重音候选** | **05:19.925–05:19.948** | 完整音轨均值、完整音轨中位数与打击声部分别给出 319.924535／319.947755／319.924535 秒；能量上升约 5.7–5.9 dB。P95 下跨方法一致，声学证据中等 |
142	| 较弱的最终收尾起音候选 | **05:25.985** | 全曲均值包络放宽到 P90 时为 325.984943 秒，能量上升约 9.7 dB，但绝对能量较低；在 P95 下不成立。若“最后重音”包含这类弱收尾，则需听辨后确认，置信较低 |
143	| 仅凭谱通量会得到的更晚峰 | 05:26.867 | 部分方法出现 326.867302 秒峰，但前后能量下降约 6 dB，不满足本报告的重音判据 |
144	
145	阈值敏感性必须保留：P97 下，完整音轨中位数方法的最后合格强起音提前到 **05:10.195**；均值及打击声部仍为 **05:19.925**。因此目前可供 MV 参考的“最后明显重音”为约 **05:19.94**，不能称作已经听辨确认的唯一最后一音。报告同时保留 05:25.985 的候选，避免把后续声音遗漏。

1	# 《嘉宾》纸艺开场样图
2	
3	[02-纸艺拼贴.png](02-纸艺拼贴.png)：1920×1080 PNG，由 Canvas 2D 代码绘制，未使用图像生成模型。
4	
5	## 画面
6	
7	依据 `song.md` 的主题“在旧爱的婚礼上承认亲密关系已结束”，以及开场情绪“分手后第几个冬季”和“拿着喜帖一步一步走近”。
8	
9	| 元素 | 含义 |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| 背对画面的 Clawd，停在路中央 | 走到一半、不愿再靠近；身后有脚印，身前没有 |
12	| Clawd 和礼堂之间的一大片雪地 | 关系的距离，是全图最空的区域 |
13	| 亮着金色窗户的礼堂、彩旗和花门 | “他精心布置的场地”，全图的暖色都集中在这里 |
14	| 钟楼里的金色小钟 | 预告第二段主歌的“钟声响起” |
15	| 红金纸屑混入雪片 | 只在礼堂一侧出现，飘到 Clawd 这边就只剩雪 |
16	| Clawd 手中的红纸与前景的大喜帖 | 同一张喜帖的两种尺度，红色只给这条叙事线和喜庆布置 |
17	| 席卡上的“嘉宾” | 全图唯一的词；画面文字只有“囍”和“嘉宾”三个字 |
18	
19	配色是灰蓝天空、米白雪地和牛皮纸棕，亮度均值 185.8（0–255）。
20	
21	## 纸艺规则
22	
23	- 底纹：牛皮纸底在四周露出；天空、远山和喜帖衬底用旧报纸。报纸只有假字条和半调网点，没有可读文字。
24	- 边缘：天空、山、雪地、路和雪堆用撕纸毛边；Clawd、礼堂、喜帖等用剪纸白边。
25	- 角色：Clawd 的几何来自 `assets/clawd/character.js` 的背面 `hold` 姿势，手臂长度不变；手中的道具只把车票配色换成喜帖红。
26	- 层次：每张纸都有投影，投影随高度加大；画面共 16 个图层。
27	- 动画：每秒更新 10 次；除牛皮纸底以外，各层每次在两个轴上独立随机抖动 1–2 像素。
28	
29	样图是不抖动的静态状态。预览动画：打开 `index.html?play`。
30	
31	## 重现
32	
33	```bash
34	node 嘉宾/开场样图/render.mjs
35	```
36	
37	```bash
38	node --test 嘉宾/开场样图/scene.test.mjs
39	```
40	
41	渲染需要本机 Chrome 和系统字体 Songti SC。脚本读取画布像素做数值检查，结果写入 [验证结果.json](验证结果.json)。未通过时不写 PNG。

# 《會呼吸的痛》MV 分鏡

狀態：使用者已於 2026-11-01 確認整體分鏡。畫面以 `MV/分鏡/` 的 41 張圖像分鏡為準；因 Clawd 的手保持設計稿長度而調整的動作，列在 `MV/README.md`，遇到與下文不同處以該表為準。

轉場採用方案②卡點切換；「全部相鄰鏡頭的衔接」一節逐條寫明 40 處衔接。

## 故事與製作邊界

**故事主線：分手後的 A 獨自登上東京鐵塔，才逐漸看懂 B 曾經的等待；想補償時，能完成的只剩紙上的承諾。** 觀眾最後記住的是：兩張票終於靠在一起，兩個人仍然沒有。

- 依據：同目錄 `會呼吸的痛.lrc` 的 37 行歌詞，以及 `會呼吸的痛.md` 的情緒分析、段落與實測節拍。音樂全長 04:33.043，時間零點沿用原始 M4A。
- 敘事視角沿用現有報告的戀人分手。A 為演唱視角，B 為已離開的戀人；不設定死亡、意外或第三者。
- A、B 均使用已指定的 Clawd，以固定配色及 B 的圍巾區分兩人，後續統一調用現有 `assets/clawd/character.js`。本稿用 A、B 表示角色身份，不修改角色模組；同一分鏡可供三種畫風共用。
- 現在的主場景為東京鐵塔觀景層休息區：窗外城市、靠窗雙人桌、兩張椅子、後方電梯。過去為兩人住處的雙人餐桌與玄關。冷藍夜色表示現在，暖黃室內表示過去；換時空必須由相同物件或構圖承接。
- 貫穿物件為兩張舊車票、一封 B 留下的信，以及信中夾著的雙人東京旅行計畫。信紙上有東京鐵塔與兩個小人；B 的圍巾在前奏就放在空椅上。這些物件不憑空出現。
- P02 首次露出桌面時，筆已放在信紙右下方，手機靠水杯支起、前鏡頭已開啟；舊信背面作為回信用紙，保留上方空白與兩幅淡線底稿：帶時鐘的玄關、B 眺望東京。L29、L33、L34 分別使用這些區域。手機、筆與水杯此後保留在原位，取放必須連續可見。
- 舊信與旅行計畫是兩張紙，取出後並排在桌上，計畫在左、舊信在右。I01 完全展開後，計畫始終正面朝上；L29 只翻舊信，兩張票留在計畫原處。L37 直接在計畫上並票，寫好的回信仍在旁邊，不能將兩張紙混成正反面。
- 信件與計畫只展示敘事需要的圖案或短語，不增加全屏歌詞、旁白或解說字幕。原曲完整保留，不增加遮蓋人聲的音效。
- 採用 HyperFrames 的「歌曲分段形成章節、物件串起因果、同一副歌返回主場景並加深」流程。此階段交付逐鏡文字，不建立工程、SPEC、素材或動畫。

## 時間與剪輯規則

1. **LRC 起唱欄是原始歌詞錨點，完全不改。切鏡起止欄是畫面邊界。** LRC 未提供逐句唱完時間，不把下一句起點當作已實測的人聲終點。
2. 每句使用起唱前最近的一個實測節拍開始衔接，以 LRC 起點作為該句表意錨點。提前量為 0.011–0.429 秒，沒有將歌詞或音訊移位；不要求把回手、取筆等準備擠在這段提前量內。衔接和準備可延續至起唱後，先揭露表意角色或手部，再在本句鏡頭內連續完成主要動作，不用瞬間換姿勢搶起唱點。
3. 切點取自 `節拍點.csv`，表格顯示到毫秒。節拍是剪輯參考格，並非每點都有明顯敲擊，也不代表小節首拍。後續製作依 CSV 完整精度定時，再依輸出幀率取最近影格。
4. 每句只用一鏡、一個主要動作；表情、物件原有狀態與動作的自然結果可以共同傳意。鏡內不插入另一個場景，不安排做完一件事再做另一件事。
5. 複合歌詞用同一處境同時承載兩層意思，不將 L09、L13、L23、L27、L31 或 L35 拆成多鏡。抽象意思的連續動作分布在相鄰歌詞鏡頭，各鏡只負責一個動作。
6. 全片 41 鏡：37 個歌詞鏡頭、2 個前奏鏡頭、2 個間奏鏡頭。歌詞鏡頭長度服從 LRC，不按固定秒數或每拍額外切鏡。
7. 除全片起止外，全部衔接起點都落在資料中的節拍。41 鏡是逐句敘事單位，同場可以連續拍攝跨過邊界，不必每句重設攝影機。換時空只在實物遮擋下更換背景，禁止無衔接硬切。間奏第一鏡從 01:42.702 開始，接近報告的聲學分界候選 01:42.748；這是暫定剪輯邊界，尚未聽辨確認人聲尾音，不能當成人聲終點。
8. 最後一句與尾奏共用一鏡，04:12.981 之後不延伸節拍、不再切鏡。04:21.944 的最後明顯重音候選只安排運鏡落定，不安排額外角色動作。

## 轉場方案與連續性規格

**推薦②卡點切換，以實物橫掃與同場動作延續銜接，不使用甩鏡。** 報告實測約 112 BPM，半速感約 56 BPM；逐句鏡頭約 3–9 秒，足以承載吸氣、走動與等待。節拍只用來啟動衔接，句內保留安靜畫面，不增加切鏡密度。

- **不選①一鏡到底**：鐵塔、住處、玄關與手機畫面之間沒有連續空間可穿行；三版幀率只有 12、10、8 fps，長距離連續運鏡會變成明顯的跳步。
- **不選③拼貼快切**：每 0.5–1 秒換畫，一句會被切成 3–18 張，放不下「一句一個動作」與半速約 56 BPM 的慢速情緒。
- **畫風適配**：像素版逐格移動整數像素；紙藝版讓有白邊、投影的實物掃過；蜡筆版保留物件筆觸。三版共用同一份幾何、相機與節拍。
- **兩種衔接**：14 處換時空或換畫面用「實物橫掃」，26 處同場用「延續」。全片沒有無衔接的硬切、整屏叠化、甩鏡或晃鏡。
- **實物橫掃**：不透明實物從節拍 t 起由右向左橫掃，歷時 0.534 秒（約一拍），行至一半時蓋滿全屏，背景只在此刻更換，不用透明度混合。實物必須是前一格已在畫面或場景內的物件。
- **同場延續**：t 前後相機與角色不變。轉身、舉手、換表情都從 t 的下一拍才開始，不與邊界同一格發生。
- **相接影格**：下表的座標都可核算。「相機 (cx, cy, z)」是場景座標的畫面中心與放大倍數；「A／B (x, y, 邊長)」是角色在 320×180 畫面上的方框。寫「前 → 後」時，方框仍必須相同，靠揭露格的相機換算達成。揭露後才連續移到本鏡目標構圖，通常兩拍內完成，且在該鏡關鍵畫面之前結束，已確認的關鍵畫面不變。
- **角色只在一側**：過去的 B 不進入現在，現在的 A 不進入 I02 的空位。這類角色只在全屏遮擋期間留在原時空，其他情況必須經畫緣或可見移動進出；A 與 B 的手不互相替換。
- **推拉次數**：沿下表執行後，推與拉的方向全片變換 21 次，平均約 13 秒一次；每次都對應一個物件特寫及返回，連續運鏡不短於兩拍。最接近的是 L29 推近信紙、L30 拉回，相隔約 4 秒，因兩鏡動作都需要，予以保留。
- **場景與道具**：雙人桌、窗、椅子、電梯、城市與桌上物件在該時空首次入鏡前已備妥，推拉只改可見範圍。信背面只在可見翻面後使用；圍巾自 L30 起留在 A 身前；手機與筆取放後留在實際位置；路人的衣袖自 L34 畫緣露出，再於 L35 伸近。
- **製作驗收**：逐處保留 t 前後與蓋滿全屏前後的連續影格，核對角色方框、相機與道具接點；逐格播放推拉段，核對物件只經畫緣、遮擋或可見取放進出。目前已檢查時間、座標資料與接縫抽幀（`.agent/visual/轉場接縫.png`），尚未生成動畫。

## 情緒弧線

| 階段 | 觀眾獲得的資訊 | 情緒與鏡頭變化 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 前奏、L01–L04 | 原本是兩人的東京約定，如今只有 A 抵達 | 城市廣景逐步收到手中兩張票，空位成為痛點 |
| L05–L06 | B 曾願意等，最後仍選擇結束關係 | 暖色回憶首次出現，以歸還鑰匙交代分手 |
| L07–L14 | 想念侵入呼吸、四肢、歌與信 | 回到現在，鏡距收緊；第一次伸向空位 |
| 間奏、L15–L20 | A 看懂 B 沒說出口的脆弱，以及自己曾忽略的訊號 | 同一封信引出更完整的回憶，責任由抽象變具體 |

| L29–L34 | A 願意坦白、擁抱、準時和陪伴 | 動作短暫變得主動，承諾仍留在無法寄出的信紙上 |
| L35–L37、尾奏 | A 仍害怕接近，也仍希望 B 回來 | 從蜷縮回到打開的雙人構圖；以空椅保留未獲回答的願望 |

11	```js
12	import {drawCharacter} from './assets/clawd/character.js';
13	
14	drawCharacter(ctx, {
15	  x: 100, y: 80, scale: 4,
16	  facing: 'right', expression: 'shy',
17	  action: 'hold', prop: 'flower', frame: 0,
18	});
19	```
20	
21	| 参数 | 取值与约定 |
22	| --- | --- |
23	| `ctx` | Canvas 2D context |
24	| `x`, `y` | 32 px 基准网格的左上原点；整数，默认 0 |
25	| `scale` | 正整数像素倍率，默认 1 |
26	| `facing` | `front`、`right`、`left`、`back`；默认 `front` |
27	| `expression` | `neutral`、`happy`、`shy`、`sad`；默认 `neutral`；背面隐藏表情 |
28	| `action` | `idle`、`walk`、`jump`、`hug`、`hold`；默认 `idle` |
29	| `frame` | 非负整数，按 4 帧循环；使用固定离散姿势，不读取时钟或随机数 |
30	| `prop` | `hold` 时支持 `ticket`、`flower`、`suitcase`，默认 `ticket`；其他动作必须为空 |
31	
32	函数返回 `bounds`、`face`、`grip`、`propGrip`、`propBounds`，坐标单位与输入相同，位于调用者当前画布变换之前。持物时道具可能超出 32 px 基准网格，排版使用实际 `bounds` 留出空间。手与道具共用握点并一起移动，所有道具位于面部下方。双角色拥抱使用两次调用，让左右侧 `hug` 姿势相向靠近；示例见 [character-sheet.html](character-sheet.html)。

1	# Storyboard recipe — plan a video as stills the person approves
2	
3	Use it whenever a run makes or changes a storyboard: when the person asks for one, or when you want their go on the shots before animating. This file owns **how to make the board**; `storyboard-format.md` owns the `STORYBOARD.md` file the tools parse.
4	
5	A film's shots are planned in the SHOTS line of `SPEC.md` (`spec.md`); a storyboard turns those shots into stills when the person wants to approve them first, one frame per shot, carrying its `reads` and `sound` (`storyboard-format.md`).
6	
7	The person sees the plan as stills on the board, comments or draws on a frame, and says go. The board is `boards/storyboard.html`, and tools that show it find its frames by the classes in § 2; boxes marked any other way (`cell` boxes, `id="frame-NN"` markers) are not found.
8	
9	## 1. The run
10	
11	1. **Pose each shot** in the composition the project renders, the root `index.html`, at its key moment: real words, real fonts, real colors, the focal point big enough to read on a phone. A shot posed in its own file (`compositions/frames/NN-*.html`) shows only once it is mounted in `index.html` (`data-composition-src`) at its planned start; `snapshot` renders `index.html` and nothing else. Before the first pose, copy `index.html` to `boards/.film.html`: until the go, the preview plays that film, never the stills (step 4).
12	2. **Snapshot every still in one run** with your host's snapshot tool when one is offered (each shot's seconds, out `boards/stills`); otherwise `npx hyperframes snapshot --at <every shot's seconds, in film order> --no-end --describe false -o boards/stills`. Each still is named `frame-NN-at-<seconds>s.png`, NN its place in the film. Every `snapshot` run clears its `-o` folder and numbers from `00`, so never snapshot a single moment into `boards/stills/` itself (step 5). Look at every still yourself; fix and snapshot again until each one holds.
13	3. **Write `boards/storyboard.html`** (§ 2), styled as a finished board: Inter or the system sans-serif, a light page, each frame a rounded card with its still above its words, even gaps.
14	4. **Put the film back.** Copy the posed `index.html` to `boards/.posed.html`, then `boards/.film.html` back over `index.html`. The board stays on its own page: held stills in the preview read as a slideshow.
15	5. **Stop.** Hand the person the board and wait for their go. Notes on frames change only those frames. For each one: copy `boards/.posed.html` over `index.html`, re-pose it, snapshot just its moment into `boards/stills/redo/` (`--at <its seconds>`), move that one file over the frame's old still under the old name (its new time in the name if the time changed, and the page's `src` with it), then put the film back (step 4), rewrite the page and stop again. The other stills stay as approved.
16	6. **Once they say go**, copy `boards/.posed.html` over `index.html` and animate from the approved stills.
17	
18	## 2. The page
19	
20	One `class="frame"` box per still, in film order, holding its image, a `class="title"` line "<two-digit number>: <name>" and a `class="time"` range in seconds. Optional: a `class="words"` line under it, and a `class="act"` heading before the first frame of each act.
21	
22	```html
23	<section class="act">Act 1: The hook</section>
24	<div class="frame">
25	  <img src="stills/frame-00-at-1.5s.png" alt="" />
26	  <div class="title">01: The hook</div>
27	  <div class="time">0.0 to 3.0s</div>
28	  <p class="words">The cursor drops the photo on the timeline; the title lands on the drop.</p>
29	</div>
30	```
31	
32	Stills are written next to the page (`boards/stills/`), so `src` is relative to `boards/` and names the file `snapshot` wrote for that shot. A still written after the page shows by itself; never reopen or rename the page for it.
33	
34	## 3. The plan beside it
35	
36	`STORYBOARD.md` at the project root (format: `storyboard-format.md`) names the same frames in the same order, and its words win over the page's: one heading per frame like `## Frame 1: The hook (0-3s)`, a `- act:` bullet for its act, and `- status: outline` until its still is posed.

## user · 2026-11-02T13:31:04Z

1	# Storyboard format — `STORYBOARD.md` + parsed manifest
2	
3	Defines the storyboard's **base data format** only: the `STORYBOARD.md` file shape and the `StoryboardManifest` it parses into. Planning the film itself is in [story.md](story.md); the optional narration/TTS file (`SCRIPT.md`) is a separate concern, not here.
4	
5	A storyboard is the **plan layer** for a video — an ordered set of **frames** (key moments) in one markdown file. Parser: `@hyperframes/core/storyboard` → `StoryboardManifest`.
6	
7	## Frontmatter (global direction)
8	
9	YAML block at the top. Unknown keys are kept under `globals.extra`.
10	
11	| Key        | Meaning                                                      | Example                                   |
12	| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
13	| `format`   | Canvas size                                                  | `1920x1080`                               |
14	| `duration` | The length the person asked for (advisory, not a hard limit) | `22s`                                     |
15	| `message`  | One-line thesis                                              | `Ship a launch video in an afternoon`     |
16	| `arc`      | Narrative arc                                                | `Hook → Problem → Solution → Proof → CTA` |
17	| `audience` | Who it's for                                                 | `indie devs on X`                         |
18	| `mode`     | Interaction mode (default collaborative)                     | `autonomous`                              |
19	
20	Set `duration` when the storyboard is first written. It is an expectation, not a gate: compare where the cut actually lands against it — judge whether the drift serves the piece, and update the value when the intended length genuinely changes.
21	
22	## Per-frame sections
23	
24	One `## Frame N — Title` heading per frame (`Frame` / `Beat` / `Scene` accepted at H2/H3). Metadata as `- key: value` bullets; everything below them until the next heading is the free-form **narrative**.
25	
26	| Key             | Meaning                                                                                                             |
27	| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
28	| `status`        | `outline` → `built` → `animated` (defaults `outline`)                                                               |
29	| `src`           | project-relative path to the frame's HTML sub-composition (the tile poster renders from it)                         |
30	| `duration`      | e.g. `4s`                                                                                                           |
31	| `transition_in` | `crossfade` / `cut` / `wipe` … (alias `transition`); a note only, build it yourself (overlap clips for a crossfade) |
32	| `scene`         | one-line contact-sheet caption (aliases `description` / `summary` / `caption`)                                      |
33	| `voiceover`     | the frame's narration _guide_ (aliases `vo` / `voice_over` / `narration`)                                           |
34	| `poster`        | seconds to seek for the tile poster (past the intro animation)                                                      |
35	| _any other key_ | kept verbatim under the frame's `extra` — carry your own per-frame data (effects, assets, …) here                   |
36	
37	Two `extra` keys every film plan carries, so the build and the review check the same thing:
38	
39	| Key     | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
40	| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
41	| `reads` | what the viewer must understand in this frame, in order, each with its window: `the cursor finds the button (0.4-1.2s); "Export" lands (1.2-2.6s)`. Windows never overlap, and each is long enough for its words (`story.md` §6) |
42	| `sound` | the bed, the effects on visible actions, or silence: `bed enters strong; click on Export; whoosh on the cut`                                                                                                                     |
43	
44	## Parsed manifest
45	
46	The parser is **lenient**: it never throws and records anything surprising as a `warning`.
47	
48	```
49	StoryboardManifest {
50	  globals: { format?, message?, arc?, audience?, extra: {…} }
51	  frames: Array<{
52	    index, number?, title?,
53	    status,                       // "outline" | "built" | "animated"
54	    src?, duration? / durationSeconds?, transitionIn?,
55	    scene?, voiceover?, poster?,
56	    narrative,                    // markdown below the metadata
57	    extra: {…}                    // unknown keys, preserved
58	  }>
59	  warnings: Array<{ message, line?, frameIndex? }>
60	}
61	```
62	
63	## `SCRIPT.md` (out of scope here)
64	
65	Optional, free-form, **not parsed into the manifest** — the locked-narration file that drives TTS, absent for videos with no narration/TTS. The per-frame `voiceover` above is the storyboard's own narration guide.
66	
67	## Example
68	
69	```markdown
70	---
71	format: 1920x1080
72	message: "Ship a launch video in an afternoon"
73	arc: Hook → Problem → Solution → Proof → CTA
74	audience: indie devs on X
75	---
76	
77	## Frame 1 — Hook
78	
79	- scene: Big type punches in on the beat
80	- duration: 3s
81	- poster: 2s
82	- transition_in: cut
83	- status: animated
84	- voiceover: "Ship a launch video in an afternoon."
85	- reads: "Ship a launch video" lands (0.3-1.6s); "in an afternoon" (1.6-3.0s)
86	- sound: bed enters on its strongest bar; impact on "afternoon"
87	- src: compositions/frames/01-hook.html
88	
89	Open cold on the promise. This is the thesis — everything after pays it off.
90	
91	## Frame 2 — The problem
92	
93	- scene: A 20-minute timer spins on a stack of rejected takes
94	- duration: 4s
95	- transition_in: crossfade
96	- status: built
97	- voiceover: "The old way? Prompt, wait twenty minutes, get something that misses."
98	- src: compositions/frames/02-problem.html
99	
100	The old way: prompt, wait, get something that misses. Establish the pain we remove.
101	```
102	
103	## Notes
104	
105	- A frame with `status: outline` and no built `src` renders as an outline placeholder.
106	- `built` is the middle rung: the frame's HTML exists and its **layout is confirmed** (a wireframe sketch or better) — motion not yet added. Nothing is drawn yet beyond the approved layout.
107	- Multi-line `voiceover` values collapse to one line on save.
108

1	# Music videos and films cut to a track
2	
3	The song is the structure. Timing facts (hits, beat trust, loops) are in `../film.md` "On music"; this file is the shape.
4	
5	## Song structure becomes edit structure
6	
7	- Find the sections first: `npx hyperframes audio <track> --only sections,onsets,moments --json`. Each section is a chapter: intro, verse, chorus, bridge, outro.
8	- Cut density follows energy: slower shots in verses, one picture per strong beat in the chorus, a held image on a breakdown.
9	- The chorus returns to one home stage and escalates each time it comes back; the ending rhymes with the opening.
10	- Chapter breaks land on section boundaries, with a transition that belongs to the film's medium (a brush wipe, a paper tear, a match cut).
11	
12	## Pictures for the words
13	
14	- Each lyric line or phrase gets its own picture (shots of about 1.4–4 s): show what the line means, not the line itself. Lyrics on screen only when asked; then each line holds at least a beat and is set as type, not subtitles.
15	- Something happens in every shot, and every cut has a cause on screen.
16	- A song about something real gets real material (footage, photos, places); an abstract track gets one world with a strong medium.
17	
18	## The look
19	
20	A physical medium carries a music film further than effects: watercolour with ink outlines, cut paper, risograph print, film grain on footage. Characters, if any, act (`character.md`).
21	
22	## Tells for this type
23	
24	The same treatment for more than about 6 s; a spectrum bar or waveform as the main picture; every cut on every beat; words about the music rather than the song's own world.
25

## user · 2026-11-02T13:31:07Z

1	# Story
2	
3	Read before building any video that tells something over about 15 s: a launch or promo, an explainer, a pull-request or changelog video, a recap, a music video with a narrative. Most weak films are good motion around no story: a list of features, three cards in a row, a logo, a URL.
4	
5	Skip it for an edit to an existing project, captions or overlays on footage, and a short single-idea piece (one kinetic line, a map move, a highlight on an image), where the request is the story. When the person gave a script, a storyboard or a reference film, follow theirs. The shape of each kind of film (launch, explainer, music, data, vertical, 3D, character) is in `types/`.
6	
7	## 1. The one thing
8	
9	- **What it is**, in one line: "You can now …" for a launch, the one idea the viewer must understand for an explainer, what changed and why it matters for a pull request. A whole release ("2.0", "what's new") is not one thing: take its headline.
10	- **The one thing to remember** after the film ends, in the viewer's words, not the brand slogan.
11	- **One viewer doing one real task**, from the moment they need it to the result. That task is the spine, and one real piece of data (a query, a file, a prompt, a number) travels through it from the hook to the payoff. An explainer's spine is one concrete example worked through.
12	- Keep facts (what it does, real numbers, real labels) apart from creative choices (angle, tone, look). Every claim on screen traces to the source: the site, the PR, the docs or the person's words. Use the person's own copy verbatim.
13	- What the source does not say stays unsaid: never derive a claim it did not make ("40 min to 2 min" is not "20× faster"), mark an example number as illustrative, and show a screen you cannot get as a labelled placeholder, not a drawn one.
14	
15	## 2. Three storylines, then one
16	
17	Write three. They are three different films, not three titles on one film: each has its own **world** (where it happens and what it looks like), its own **device** (what the story is) and its own **form** (how the camera and the cuts carry it). Sketch five or more ideas first, a line each pairing a device with a form (tables below); drop those the subject cannot carry well, and of the rest keep the three that differ most. Make one of the three the bold one you would not have picked first. Each says:
18	
19	- its name, its device and form in a few words, and in two sentences what the viewer sees and feels;
20	- the first two seconds, exactly;
21	- its beats in one line (`hook → … → end card`);
22	- its look in one line: ground, type, the one material or treatment, taken from the subject or the brand (`look.md`);
23	- its sound in one line (`sound.md` §1).
24	
25	The storylines are words: build nothing for any of them before one is picked. Pick a storyline for its story: the one a stranger would follow and remember, with people or a situation they know, ahead of the most striking picture. Picking a storyline picks its look and its sound. Then write the picked one as `SPEC.md`.
26	
27	Put your recommendation first, with the reason in one clause, and save all three in the project as `STORYLINES.md` so a later turn can switch.
28	
29	- **The person is there to answer:** show the three and stop once until they pick. A mix ("A's opening with C's middle") is one storyline. Ask nothing else unless only they can answer it (real screens you cannot capture, narrated or music only). State everything else in one assumption line: the length as a range, the aspect, music or voice, and every paid item (a HeyGen voice, an avatar, catalog music) with the free option beside it.
30	- **They asked for the file or for no stops:** take your recommendation, build it, and name the other two in one line each in your reply.
31	- With a storyboard (`storyboard.md`), the picked storyline becomes the board's frames.
32	
33	| Device                        | What the viewer sees                                                                    |
34	| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
35	| A moment in someone's day     | a person, a time stamp, the message that creates the need ("launch is tomorrow")        |
36	| A character does the work     | a mascot or a cursor carries, drags, draws and reacts; every cut has a cause            |
37	| The feature as the hook       | the feature happening to a recognisable image in the first half second                  |
38	| The result first              | the finished output plays, then the camera pulls back to show where it came from        |
39	| One object across apps        | the thing being made travels from one app into the product, which keeps working on it   |
40	| Life before and after         | the old way as a scene (one person drowning in tabs), then the new way                  |
41	| Type carries the argument     | giant kinetic type, colour fields and grids that cut on the beat                        |
42	| A number lands                | one real number earned by a scene, then made physical                                   |
43	| A question with the input     | "What if you could make a video from your ⟨website⟩?", the blank filled by a real input |
44	| The object is the explanation | a machine or model whose working is the idea; the camera tours through it               |
45	
46	| Form                       | What the viewer sees                                                                         |
47	| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
48	| One continuous take        | the camera never cuts; it pushes, pulls and travels from one world into the next             |
49	| Object-to-object chain     | every shot ends on the thing that opens the next: a button becomes a card becomes a phone    |
50	| An endless zoom            | the camera dives into a detail that turns out to be the next world, again and again          |
51	| A flight through one world | a 3D set, a map or a desk the camera travels across; each idea is a stop on the route        |
52	| Cut on the beat            | hard cuts on the music, type and colour fields changing every half beat                      |
53	| Match cuts                 | one shape holds while everything around it changes: a circle becomes a lens, a wheel, a logo |
54	| Split screen to one        | several panes play at once, then collapse into the one that matters                          |
55	| One frame that rebuilds    | a single composition keeps rearranging itself and never leaves the frame                     |
56	
57	A pitch where all three are plain cuts between scenes has not tried the forms. Before and after: the new side moves calmly while the old side churns; never mock a named competitor. A recap asks one question first so each piece answers it.
58	
59	## 3. The hook
60	
61	The first two seconds are the densest of the film, and frame 0 is the thumbnail: never black, never a logo alone. Open on the feature working on something recognisable, a real moment that creates the need, a question with the input inside it, a sentence whose last word becomes the picture, or the bug itself. Then let the old way fail on screen (the wait, the wall of text, the wrong result) before the product brings relief; the proof is often the same shot improved in front of the viewer. Typing into a prompt box as the opener, with nothing else on screen, is the tell of a generated film; as a story step a few seconds in, it is fine.
62	
63	## 4. Beats
64	
65	A common shape for a launch of about 35 s; scale it, let the device bend it, and take another type's shape from its file in `types/`:
66	
67	| Beat     | Share | Job                                                                                       |
68	| -------- | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
69	| Hook     | ~8%   | the world and the need, or the feature already working                                    |
70	| Tension  | ~12%  | the old way failing on screen, or a gag                                                   |
71	| Reveal   | ~8%   | the product or idea named as a title, about 20–30% in                                     |
72	| Proof    | ~40%  | the real task in the real UI as 3–6 verbs (_paste, pick, watch it build, ship_), one each |
73	| Payoff   | ~20%  | the output arrives, already moving: the biggest visual moment, once, 60–80% in            |
74	| Claim    | ~8%   | the one thing, in one line                                                                |
75	| End card | ~8%   | the mark carried in, the name and the call to action land and hold 2–3 s                  |
76	
77	In each verb beat keep only what the cursor touches and what proves the line; delete the rest of the screen. The process runs fast; the payoff plays at normal speed. Length follows the story (a feature launch is usually 20–45 s); a length in the request is a range, never padded.
78	
79	## 5. Worlds
80	
81	A film visits several worlds, each with its own background, light and scale (a desktop, the product on a brand gradient, a white void with a character, live action), never one dark canvas with small UI floating in it. Enter each world through an object already on screen: the thing clicked becomes the next shot. Keep one home stage to return to, one carrier the eye follows, and the palette and type constant across worlds.
82	
83	## 6. Copy and voice
84	
85	- Titles take at most 6 words a line, one line on screen at a time, no trailing periods; an explainer's lines may run to about 10. A line holds about 0.3 s a word plus 0.5 s, and the last line at least 2 s.
86	- Show, don't list: no bullet slides or three-card rows. When similar things repeat, each gets its own idea and layout.
87	- Real numbers only, from the source. The first line is never "Introducing", "Meet" or the logo; after the pain, "Introducing X" is fine. Never "unlock", "seamless", "supercharge", "game-changer", "revolutionize", "effortless", or "in seconds" unless measured.
88	- Read the lines alone: a stranger gets the pitch. Watch the pictures alone: they tell the same story.
89	- No voiceover unless the request or the source calls for one; then the screen never repeats the spoken sentence word for word. Without a voice, large titles and the product's own text carry the words, over music and effects (`sound.md`).
90	
91	## 7. The brand
92	
93	The mark lands once, with weight, usually on the end card; before it the brand shows only inside the product and the story, never docked small in a corner. The end card is built, not a still: the mark is carried in, typed or wiped in. The accent colour is rationed: one highlighted word, the payoff, the end card.
94	
95	## 8. Tells of a generated film
96	
97	The defaults a film falls into when nothing is decided are banned by name in `spec.md` ("BANNED by default"): a dark void with small things floating in it, glow and particles, the cream-paper-serif-mono-label look, everything fading and sliding up, three cards in a row, the docked logo. Beyond those, for a story:
98	
99	- every scene entering the same way, or the same move beat after beat;
100	- side-by-side panels and floating cards standing in for a scene;
101	- titles that keep sliding or shrinking after they land; breathing or floating loops standing in for motion on titles and UI (a character's idle breath is acting, `types/character.md`).
102	
103	When a first render shows any of them, name which, take the replacement from the subject, the brand or the medium, and add it to the BANNED line of `SPEC.md`.
104

1	---
2	name: hyperframes
3	description: Read first to make, edit, animate or render any video with HyperFrames (HTML rendered to video), including launch films, explainers, music videos, charts, maps, vertical clips, title cards, captions and overlays. Holds the render contract, the work loop and what each kind of video needs.
4	---
5	
6	**Plugin installs:** Before setup or freshness commands, follow [plugin execution rules](references/plugin-installation.md) when this skill is inside a HyperFrames plugin.
7	
8	# HyperFrames
9	
10	HyperFrames renders HTML to video by seeking a paused timeline frame by frame, so every render is identical; the person edits the same files in the Studio preview. Use it unless another framework or a plain browser recording is asked for. Run the CLI as `npx hyperframes <command>` (`/hyperframes-cli`); at the start of a new video, `npx hyperframes usage --json` reports the person's remaining plan usage (say "unknown" when it is).
11	
12	`index.html` is the root composition: it declares the video's variables and mounts one scene per sub-composition from `compositions/`. Media and fonts live in `assets/`. A new project: `npx hyperframes init <dir>`. A website as the subject: `npx hyperframes capture <url> --json`.
13	
14	Build what was asked: no voiceover or captions and no new aspect ratio unless the request or the source calls for them; a film over ~15 s that tells something gets music and sound on its visible actions unless the person asked for silence (`references/sound.md`). A new video is 1920×1080 at 30 fps. A question, a hold or a loose idea gets an answer or a proposal, not an edit. Before hand-writing a named effect, transition, caption style, chart or card, search the registry (`/hyperframes-registry`). Any media (a presenter or avatar, footage, voice, music): `/media-use`, which says when HeyGen is needed and what is free. Show real things from their source (the product's screens, the brand's logo, a real place's imagery); draw only what has none.
15	
16	## Contract
17	
18	`npx hyperframes check --json` reports most violations with a `Fix:` line.
19	
20	1. Every timed element has `class="clip"`, `data-start` and `data-duration` in seconds, and shows over `[start, start + duration)`: land an end state just before its end. `data-track-index` is only a Studio lane; paint order is `z-index`.
21	2. The video's length is the root's `data-duration`: overrun is cut, an early end holds the last frame.
22	3. Each composition builds one paused timeline and registers it after its tweens: `window.__timelines["<data-composition-id>"] = tl`.
23	4. No `Date.now()`, unseeded `Math.random()`, network fetches, timers or `repeat: -1`. Everything visible is a function of timeline time.
24	5. Never tween `display`, `visibility` or `autoAlpha` on a `.clip`; animate a child.
25	6. No CSS `transform` on an element GSAP transforms; animate transforms, not `left`/`top`/`width`/`height`.
26	7. Never `play()`, `pause()` or seek media. A `<video>` keeps its sound with `data-has-audio="true"`, else it is `muted`; music, voice, replacement sound and J/L cuts are a separate `<audio>`.
27	8. Every `<audio>` has an `id` or it is left out of the mix. No `crossorigin` on media. Time a `<video>` or its wrapper, never both.
28	9. Only the bundled fonts (`references/format.md`) resolve by name; any other family needs `@font-face` to a file in `assets/fonts/`.
29	10. Asset paths: `assets/...` (no leading `/`), in sub-compositions too.
30	11. Grades, grain, blur and vignettes on footage go through `npx hyperframes media-treatment` (`/media-use`), never CSS filters.
31	12. A scene file puts its styles, markup and scripts inside `<template>` and styles its root as `#root`. Intended overflow or overlap: `data-layout-allow-overflow`, `data-layout-allow-overlap`.
32	
33	## Keep it editable
34	
35	Studio edits the tags you write.
36	
37	- One scene per sub-composition, short readable ids; the root holds only scene hosts, media and audio.
38	- Timed elements are written in the HTML, not made by script, each with a stable `id`.
39	- Copy, brand colours and swappable media are variables (`data-var-text`, `data-var-src`, `var(--id)`).
40	- One kind per track: `data-track-kind="graphics"` on scene and overlay hosts, `captions` on the one host that holds every caption group.
41	- Content stays inside the 90% action-safe box, captions and key text inside 80% title-safe; Studio draws the guides, never add them.
42	
43	## Work loop
44	
45	- An existing project: `npx hyperframes timeline --json` shows what plays when; before any change, `npx hyperframes history --since mine --who <you>` shows what the person changed since your last turn: build on it (`/hyperframes-cli`).
46	- A new film over ~15 s that tells something: its type's file (below), then `references/story.md`: three storylines that are three different films, in words only; the person picks unless they asked for the file or no stops. Then `SPEC.md` (`references/spec.md`): every adjective as a number, the defaults banned by name, the shots by frame.
47	- After your last edit: `npx hyperframes check --json`; fix every error, weigh every warning. A film: `npx hyperframes snapshot --review` and `references/review.md`, ending in `REVIEW.md`. A small edit: snapshot what you changed (`--at`, `--range`, `--composition`) and look before you reply.
48	- Render when the person approves the Studio preview, asks for the file or asks for no stops, after your check and review pass; otherwise stop at the preview and wait.
49	
50	## The HyperFrames desktop app
51	
52	Call it "the HyperFrames desktop app", never "Studio"; offer it as the better way to keep editing, not the only one.

};

}

}

  "content": "import bisect\nimport csv\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / '嘉宾'\n\n\ndef fmt(t):\n    m = int(t // 60)\n    return f'{m:02d}:{t - m * 60:06.3f}'\n\n\nwith open(ROOT / '节拍点.csv', newline='') as f:\n    beats = [float(row['seconds']) for row in csv.DictReader(f)]\n\nlines = []\nfor raw in (ROOT / '嘉宾.lrc').read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines():\n    m = re.match(r'\\[(\\d+):(\\d+\\.\\d+)\\]', raw)\n    if m:\n        lines.append(int(m[1]) * 60 + float(m[2]))\n\nleads = []\nfor i, t in enumerate(lines, 1):\n    k = bisect.bisect_right(beats, t) - 1\n    leads.append(t - beats[k])\n    print(f'L{i:02d} lrc={fmt(t)} cut=#{k + 1} {fmt(beats[k])} lead={t - beats[k]:.3f}')\nprint('max lead', round(max(leads), 3), 'mean lead', round(sum(leads) / len(leads), 3))\n"

  function worldRect(px, py, width, height) {
    return {x: x + (mirror ? 32 - px - width : px) * scale, y: y + (py + lift) * scale,
      width: width * scale, height: height * scale};
  }
  function union(a, b) {
    if (!a) return b;
    const left = Math.min(a.x, b.x), top = Math.min(a.y, b.y);
    return {x: left, y: top, width: Math.max(a.x + a.width, b.x + b.width) - left,
      height: Math.max(a.y + a.height, b.y + b.height) - top};
  }
  function rect(px, py, width, height, color, isProp = false) {
    ctx.fillStyle = color;
    ctx.fillRect(px, py, width, height);
    const region = worldRect(px, py, width, height);
    bounds = union(bounds, region);
    if (isProp) propBounds = union(propBounds, region);
  }
  function hand(px, py) {
    rect(px - 1, py - 1, 3, 3, colors.outline);
    ctx.translate(x, y + lift * scale);
    ctx.scale(scale, scale);
    if (mirror) { ctx.translate(32, 0); ctx.scale(-1, 1); }

## 故事主线
Clawd 拿着喜帖去参加旧爱的婚礼，从强撑体面到离席失控，最后把自己收回来，再把对方交给另一个人。

| 段落 | 观众看到的 | 情绪 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 开场 | Clawd 停在通往礼堂的路上；回到家中，手机收到婚讯，全世界的纸片停住 | 冷清 → 错愕 |
| 副歌一 | 走近礼堂，被别上“嘉宾”胸花，把旧合照塞进礼金箱，握手很客气，新娘用红包盖住露出的相片 | 强撑、刺痛 |
| 间奏 | 回到过去的雪地，两人拉钩；再回到现实，他坐在最后一排 | 全片最暖 → 落回现实 |
| 主歌二、副歌二 | 钟响，新郎下跪，戴戒指；红线连遍全场，只漏掉他；笑脸纸片掉落，他从侧门离开 | 上升至失控 |
| 桥段 | 雪地露出是纸舞台，他自己把幕布拉上 | 自嘲 |
| 终副歌 | 隔窗旁观，眼泪变成旧照片，只冒出一个空白气泡；雪停，他抖落胸花 | 最低点 → 转向自己 |
| 结尾 | 他站到合影最边上；新人拉钩时他已转身，走回开场那条路；雪盖住脚印和席卡 | 留白 |

## 校验结果
- **时间：** 所有切点都在 `节拍点.csv` 的节拍上，每句都从自己的镜头内开始，切镜比起唱早 0.074–0.727 秒。镜头首尾相接，覆盖全曲 05:33.677。
- **朝向：** 主角入画 47 镜，46 镜是正面。新郎在走向新娘和下跪的两镜用侧面，这两镜主角不入画。
- **未验证：** 节拍是算法结果，没有经过听辨校准。动作观众能否看懂，还要等草图阶段才有依据。

## 三处和你的要求不同或需要知道
- **歌词不写入分镜：** 文件里用 L01–L46 行号和起唱时间对应 `嘉宾.lrc`，另附我转述的句意，所以看分镜时要对照 LRC。
- **无名指：** Clawd 的手没有手指，L20 的戒指直接套在手部方块上。
- **故事线：** HyperFrames 流程原本要先写三条候选故事线，但歌词已经定了人物和情节，我只写了这一条。画风沿用已选定的纸艺样图。

## 确认时请告诉我
1. **抽象歌词：** 第 4 项你还留着占位文字“(写在这里)”，所以文件里的“抽象歌词表”全是我的理解。要改的话，告诉我行号和你的理解。
2. **开场背面：** P01 沿用样图里背对画面的 Clawd，结尾在同一构图改成正面离开，形成首尾对照。如果你要全片正面，这个对照就要重新设计。
3. **歌词字幕：** 你没有提到，我暂按前几支 MV 在画面底部留了字幕区。不要字幕的话，构图也不用改。

24	// 呼吸：腿不动，躯干以腰线为基准上下伸缩。眨眼：把眼睛压成一行。
25	export function posedRects(item) {
26	  const lift = (item.breath ?? 0) * 0.045, eyes = CHARACTER_COLORS.eyes, out = [];
27	  for (const rect of clawdRects(item)) {
28	    let {y, h} = rect;
29	    if (lift && y < 21) { y -= lift * (21 - y); h = h * (1 + lift); }
30	    if (item.blink && rect.color === eyes && rect.y < 16) { if (rect.y > 13 || rect.y + rect.h <= 13) continue; y = 13; h = 1; }
31	    out.push({...rect, y, h});
32	  }
33	  return out;
34	}

1	# Composition format
2	
3	The detail behind the contract in `SKILL.md`. Full references: `npx hyperframes docs compositions`, `docs data-attributes`, `docs troubleshooting`.
4	
5	## Shape of a project
6	
7	```html
8	<!-- index.html: a normal document; declares variables, mounts scenes -->
9	<html
10	  data-composition-variables='[{"id":"headline","type":"string","label":"Headline","default":"…"}]'
11	>
12	  <body>
13	    <div
14	      id="root"
15	      data-composition-id="main"
16	      data-start="0"
17	      data-duration="12"
18	      data-width="1920"
19	      data-height="1080"
20	    >
21	      <div
22	        id="intro"
23	        data-composition-id="intro"
24	        data-composition-src="compositions/intro.html"
25	        data-start="0"
26	        data-duration="4"
27	        data-track-index="1"
28	        data-width="1920"
29	        data-height="1080"
30	      ></div>
31	    </div>
32	    <script>
33	      window.__timelines["main"] = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
34	    </script>
35	  </body>
36	</html>
37	```
38	
39	```html
40	<!-- compositions/intro.html: everything inside <template> -->
41	<template>
42	  <style>
43	    #root {
44	      position: absolute;
45	      inset: 0;
46	    }
47	  </style>
48	  <div id="root" data-composition-id="intro" data-width="1920" data-height="1080">
49	    <h1 id="headline" class="clip" data-start="0.4" data-duration="3" data-var-text="headline">
50	      …
51	    </h1>
52	  </div>
53	  <script>
54	    const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
55	    tl.fromTo(
56	      "#headline",
57	      { opacity: 0, filter: "blur(8px)" },
58	      { opacity: 1, filter: "blur(0px)", duration: 0.18, ease: "power4.out" },
59	      0.4,
60	    );
61	    window.__timelines["intro"] = tl;
62	  </script>
63	</template>
64	```
65	
66	- Give the host, the scene root and the timeline key the same id. A host id that differs from its scene's makes each render wait 45 s per scene, then show static frames. Styles and scripts outside `<template>` are dropped.
67	- Size the scene root with `inset: 0`, never hard-coded pixels; the canvas is `data-width` × `data-height`.
68	- Keep ids unique across the assembled page (prefix them: `#intro-title`). A scene's timeline can't reach elements outside its file.
69	- Use `fromTo`, not `from`, inside a scene: the host re-seeks the scene each time it shows, and `from` records its start state once, so it drifts on seek-back.
70	- Never `add()` a scene's timeline to the root's; the runtime drives each scene itself, and nesting seeks it twice.
71	
72	## Attributes you'll use most
73	
74	| Attribute                                      | Meaning                                                                                             |
75	| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
76	| `data-start`, `data-duration`                  | Seconds, local to the file that declares the element                                                |
77	| `data-track-index`                             | Studio lane only; paint order is CSS `z-index`                                                      |
78	| `data-track-kind`                              | `graphics` or `captions` on scene hosts (video and audio come from the tag)                         |
79	| `data-composition-src`, `data-variable-values` | Mount a scene file; per-mount variable values (a JSON object)                                       |
80	| `data-media-start`                             | Offset into the source media (a trim)                                                               |
81	| `data-playback-rate`                           | Constant speed, 0.1–10                                                                              |
82	| `data-has-audio="true"`                        | A `<video>` keeps its own sound; a timed `<video>` with neither this nor `muted` fails lint         |
83	| `data-volume`, `data-fade-in`, `data-fade-out` | Gain (1 = 0 dB, up to 3.98 = +12 dB) and edge fades; envelopes use `data-automation` (`/media-use`) |
84	| `data-link`, `data-sync-origin`                | A video and audio edited as one (see Linked clips)                                                  |
85	| `data-hidden`                                  | Hidden in preview and render; reversible                                                            |
86	| `data-no-timeline`                             | On the root of a still composition: no timeline to wait for                                         |
87	
88	## Variables
89	
90	- Declare an array of `{id, type, label, default}`: the video's own on `index.html`'s `<html>`, a scene or block file's on that file's `<html>` (or root element), where they stay inside each mount. Types: `string` (`placeholder`, `maxLength`), `number` (`min`, `max`, `step`, `unit`), `color`, `boolean`, `enum` (`options: [{value, label}]`).
91	- Bind without script: `data-var-text="id"`, `data-var-src="id"` (keep a real fallback `src` on media with audio), `var(--id)` in CSS; for logic, `window.__hyperframes.getVariables()` once at init.
92	- Values are an object keyed by id. A host's `data-variable-values` sets one mount; Studio's Variables panel and batch renders set only the root's variables, so to vary a block, change its host's values. Variables can't change the root's `data-duration`.
93	
94	## Fonts
95	
96	- Bundled, so they resolve by name: Inter, Montserrat, Outfit, Nunito, Oswald, League Gothic, Archivo Black, Space Mono, IBM Plex Mono, JetBrains Mono, EB Garamond, Playfair Display, Source Code Pro, Noto Sans JP, Roboto, Open Sans, Lato, Poppins. Common system fonts (Helvetica, Arial, Times, Menlo and the like) are swapped for the nearest of these.
97	- The bundle only has Latin text at a few weights per family (Inter: 400, 700, 900). The compiler still fetches each of these families from Google Fonts for the other weights and scripts, and caches the result in `~/.cache/hyperframes/fonts`.
98	- Any other family needs `@font-face` in the file that uses it, or lint fails `font_family_without_font_face`: `src: url('assets/fonts/x.woff2')` for a file in the project (a capture's own fonts, or one you download there), or `local('Exact Name')` for a font installed on this machine.
99	
100	## Timing and the timeline
101	
102	- A clip shows over `[start, start + duration)`: an end state landing exactly on its end is never rendered.
103	- Only a composition's root timeline is paused; timelines nested inside it are not. Never `tl.play()`.
104	- A scene's clock starts at 0 at its host's `data-start`; media `data-start` is local to its composition. `<video>` / `<audio>` without `data-duration` play their full length; an `<img>` without one lasts 3 s.
105	- A host's `data-duration` is the scene's slot: a shorter scene timeline holds its last frame, and a slot shorter than the video goes blank when it ends.
106	- Root children with `data-start` are laid out full-frame by the runtime; an untimed full-bleed background needs `position: absolute; inset: 0` or it collapses to nothing.
107	- A fill on the composition root is dropped when the video has shader transitions or HDR media; put it on a full-bleed child.
108	- `data-start="intro + 0.5"` starts after `intro` ends (spaces required). A typo, a missing id or a cycle silently resolves to 0, so snapshot what you time this way.
109	- A clip nested inside another timed element counts its `data-start` from the composition, not from that element, and shows only while that element shows. `timeline` lists it under its parent and warns `never visible` when the windows miss (`lint`: `nested_clip_never_visible`).
110	- `npx hyperframes timeline --json` lists every clip by kind with `absStart`, `absEnd`, `file`, `src`, `playbackRate`, `nested`, `host` and `durationSource`: read it instead of opening every file. It reads one level of nesting (a deeper scene shows `children=unread`); `laneError` means a `data-automation` or `data-fx-chain` that doesn't parse.
111	
112	## Adding media
113	
114	Write what a Studio drop writes, so the clip behaves like one the person dropped:
115	
116	- `id`, `class="clip"`, `data-start` (the playhead or the requested time, never a silent 0) and `data-track-index`. Video with sound: `playsinline data-has-audio="true"`; silent footage: `muted playsinline`. Audio: `data-volume="1"`.
117	- Images and video fill the frame: `position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0`, width and height equal to the canvas, `object-fit: contain`.
118	- `z-index` is the number of top-level clips already in that file plus one.
119	- Raise the root's `data-duration` to cover the new clip's end, or it never plays.
120	
121	## Linked clips
122	
123	Studio's Detach audio writes a muted `<video>` and an `<audio>` of the same file sharing `data-link` and `data-sync-origin`; Studio moves, trims, splits and deletes them as one.
124	
125	- Prefer one `<video data-has-audio="true">`; link only when the sound needs its own track, volume or effects.
126	- Every member keeps the same `data-start`, `data-duration`, `data-media-start` and `data-playback-rate`; retime them all together.
127	- Unlink by removing `data-link` from every member. Leave `data-sync-origin` alone while they are still one source.
128	
129	## Layout audit opt-outs
130	
131	`check` measures boxes at sampled times; `overflow: hidden` does not silence a finding. Use the narrowest opt-out:
132	
133	| Attribute                        | Silences                                                                                                                 |
134	| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
135	| `data-layout-allow-overflow`     | Overflow on the element and every descendant, including text-clipping checks: keep it on the smallest decorative wrapper |
136	| `data-layout-bleed="true"`       | One intentional crop of primary text                                                                                     |
137	| `data-layout-allow-overlap`      | Deliberate text layering, on that block only (not inherited)                                                             |
138	| `data-layout-allow-occlusion`    | An element meant to cover text                                                                                           |
139	| `data-layout-allow-caption-zone` | Intentional copy in the caption band                                                                                     |
140	| `data-layout-ignore`             | A decorative element never audited                                                                                       |
141	
142	## Lint errors you'll meet first
143	
144	| Rule                                                   | Fix                                                                                                    |
145	| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
146	| `video_missing_muted`                                  | A timed `<video>` gets `data-has-audio="true"` or `muted`                                              |
147	| `gsap_css_transform_conflict`                          | Set the start inside the tween (`gsap.fromTo`) instead of a CSS `transform`                            |
148	| `gsap_animates_clip_element`                           | Animate a child of the `.clip`, or its `opacity`                                                       |
149	| `video_nested_in_timed_element`                        | Time the `<video>` or its wrapper, not both                                                            |
150	| `media_missing_id`, `media_crossorigin_breaks_preview` | Give every `<audio>` an `id`; drop `crossorigin`                                                       |
151	| `gsap_timeline_registered_before_async_build`          | Register the timeline at the end of the async callback                                                 |
152	| `standalone_composition_wrapped_in_template`           | Only scene files use `<template>`                                                                      |
153	| `subcomposition_linked_style_names_root_id`            | A linked sheet cannot style a scene's root by id: use an inline `<style>`, or select a child           |
154	| `subcomposition_root_styled_by_class`                  | Style a scene's root as `#root`                                                                        |
155	| `subcomposition_blanks_before_host`                    | Make the scene's slot span the time it should show                                                     |
156	| `clip_ends_past_root_duration`                         | Raise the root's `data-duration`                                                                       |
157	| `linked_clips_out_of_sync`, `linked_clip_orphan`       | Retime every linked member together; unlink from all of them                                           |
158	| `sweep_static`                                         | A 3 s+ video with no visible change: spread the motion, or mark a still composition `data-no-timeline` |
159	| `missing_data_no_timeline`                             | A root or host with no timeline: add `data-no-timeline`, or every render waits 45 s                    |

Compositions

A composition is an HTML document that defines a video timeline.

Structure

Every composition needs a root element with data-composition-id:

<div id="root" data-composition-id="root" data-width="1920" data-height="1080">
  <!-- Elements go here -->
</div>

Nested Compositions

Embed one composition inside another:

<div data-composition-src="./intro.html" data-start="0" data-duration="5"></div>

Listing Compositions

Use npx hyperframes compositions to see all compositions in a project.

Variables

Two attributes with different shapes and different jobs:

  • **data-composition-variables** on the <html> root — a JSON **array of declarations** ({id, type, label, default} per entry). Defines the schema: which variables exist, what type they are, and what defaults to use when no override is provided.
  • **data-variable-values** on a sub-comp host element — a JSON **object keyed by variable id** ({"title":"Pro","price":"$29"}). Carries per-instance overrides for that one mount of the sub-composition.

They aren't redundant — one is "what variables does this composition have?" and the other is "what values should this particular embed use?" Inside any composition script, window.__hyperframes.getVariables() returns the merged result. Layering, lowest to highest precedence:

1. Declared defaults from data-composition-variables
2. Per-instance overrides from the host's data-variable-values (sub-comp embeds only)
3. CLI overrides from npx hyperframes render --variables '{...}' (top-level renders only)

<!-- compositions/card.html -->
<html data-composition-variables='[
  {"id":"title","type":"string","label":"Title","default":"Hello"},
  {"id":"color","type":"color","label":"Color","default":"#111827"}
]'>
  <body>
    <div data-composition-id="card" data-width="1920" data-height="1080">
      <h1 class="title"></h1>
      <script>
        const { title, color } = window.__hyperframes.getVariables();
        document.querySelector(".title").textContent = title;
        document.querySelector(".title").style.color = color;
      </script>
    </div>

# Animation runtimes

HyperFrames seeks each frame on its own, so motion must be a function of time, never of the previous frame. Full GSAP reference: `npx hyperframes docs gsap`.

## GSAP facts that bite

- Register the timeline last. Building inside `document.fonts.ready.then(…)` or another async callback is fine if you register at the end of it; registering first renders blank (`gsap_timeline_regis
- Place tweens at absolute seconds (`tl.to(el, {…}, 2.4)`). Set start states in the tween (`fromTo`), not in CSS.
- Measure layout once before building tweens, never inside `onUpdate`.
- Finite repeats only: `repeat: Math.max(0, Math.floor(duration / cycle) - 1)`.
- Seed randomness with a small PRNG (mulberry32).
- A scene's timeline can't reach elements outside its file, and two timelines must not animate the same property of one element.
- Transforms on a `<span>` need `display: inline-block` or `block`.
- Text that must fit a width: `window.__hyperframes.fitTextFontSize(text, { fontFamily, fontWeight, maxWidth })` returns `{ fontSize }`; `window.__hyperframes.pretext` measures text without a reflow.

## Other runtimes

| Runtime                      | Use for                           | How HyperFrames drives it                                                                        |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| CSS `@keyframes`             | Simple loops and decoration       | Found automatically; finite iterations, `animation-fill-mode: both`, `data-start` on the element |
| WAAPI                        | Native keyframes                  | `element.animate(…, { fill: "both" })` then `pause()`; times are document time, so use `delay`   |
| Lottie / dotLottie           | After Effects exports, characters | `autoplay: false`, always set `loop`, push the instance to `window.__hfLottie`                   |
| anime.js v4                  | Existing anime code               | `autoplay: false`, push to `window.__hfAnime`, `anime.createSeededRandom`                        |
| Three.js, WebGPU, p5, canvas | 3D and generative                 | Draw from `e.detail.time` in an `hf-seek` listener; set `data-duration` on the root              |

Charts and map overlays: drive them from a GSAP tween's `onUpdate`, not the library's own transitions. A real place is shown on baked imagery, not drawn (`film.md` "Maps and real places"). Heavy setup

## dotLottie browser setup

Copy `dist/index.js` and `dist/dotlottie-player.wasm` from the same pinned
`@lottiefiles/dotlottie-web` release (for example, 0.81.0) into the project's
`lib/dotlottie-web/` directory. Its CommonJS entry cannot run as a classic
browser script. Import the ESM entry and set the local WASM URL before creating
the player, so rendering loads the SDK, WASM and animation from project files.

```html
<canvas id="anim" style="width:100%;height:100%"></canvas>
<script type="module">
  import { DotLottie } from "./lib/dotlottie-web/index.js";

import {readFile, mkdir, mkdtemp, rm} from 'node:fs/promises';
import path from 'node:path';
import {fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';

export const here = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
export const root = path.resolve(here, '../../..');
const CHROME = process.env.CHROME || '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome';
const MIME = {'.html': 'text/html', '.js': 'text/javascript', '.mjs': 'text/javascript'};

export async function openChrome() {
  const server = createServer(async (req, res) => {
    try {
      const file = path.join(root, decodeURIComponent(new URL(req.url, 'http://x').pathname));
      if (!file.startsWith(root)) throw new Error('outside root');
      const body = await readFile(file);
      res.writeHead(200, {'content-type': MIME[path.extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream'});
      res.end(body);
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); }
  });
  await new Promise(ok => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', ok));
  const port = server.address().port;

  await mkdir(path.join(root, '.agent/work'), {recursive: true});
  const profile = await mkdtemp(path.join(root, '.agent/work/opening-chrome-'));
  const chrome = spawn(CHROME, ['--headless=new', '--remote-debugging-port=0', `--user-data-dir=${profile}`,
    '--window-size=1920,1080', '--force-device-scale-factor=1', '--use-angle=swiftshader', '--enable-unsafe-swiftshader',
    '--ignore-gpu-blocklist', '--no-first-run', 'about:blank'], {stdio: ['ignore', 'ignore', 'pipe']});
  const wsUrl = await new Promise((ok, fail) => {
    let log = '';
    chrome.stderr.on('data', d => { log += d; const m = log.match(/ws:\/\/\S+/); if (m) ok(m[0]); });
    chrome.once('exit', code => fail(new Error(`Chrome 退出 ${code}: ${log}`)));
  });

  const ws = new WebSocket(wsUrl);
  await new Promise((ok, fail) => { ws.onopen = ok; ws.onerror = fail; });
  let id = 0;
  const pending = new Map();
  ws.onmessage = e => {
    const msg = JSON.parse(e.data);
    if (msg.id && pending.has(msg.id)) { pending.get(msg.id)(msg); pending.delete(msg.id); }
  };
  const send = (method, params = {}, sessionId) => new Promise((ok, fail) => {
    const n = ++id;
    pending.set(n, msg => (msg.error ? fail(new Error(`${method}: ${msg.error.message}`)) : ok(msg.result)));
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({id: n, method, params, sessionId}));
  });

  const {targetId} = await send('Target.createTarget', {url: 'about:blank'});
  const {sessionId} = await send('Target.attachToTarget', {targetId, flatten: true});
  const page = (method, params) => send(method, params, sessionId);
  const evaluate = async expression => {
    const r = await page('Runtime.evaluate', {expression, awaitPromise: true, returnByValue: true});
    if (r.exceptionDetails) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(r.exceptionDetails));
    return r.result.value;
  };
  await page('Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride', {width: 1920, height: 1080, deviceScaleFactor: 1, mobile: false});

  async function openStyle(style, dir = here) {
    await page('Page.navigate', {url: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/${encodeURI(path.relative(root, dir))}/index.html?style=${style}`});
    let state = {};
    for (let i = 0; i < 2400; i++) {
      await new Promise(ok => setTimeout(ok, 250));
      state = await evaluate(`({ready: !!window.artReady && location.search.includes('style=${style}'), errors: window.renderErrors || []})`).catch(()
      if (state.ready || state.errors.length) break;
    }
    if (!state.ready || state.errors.length) throw new Error(`${style} 未完成: ${JSON.stringify(state)}`);
  }

  "content": "// 用法：node --test 嘉宾/MV/stage.test.mjs\nimport test from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport {readFileSync} from 'node:fs';\nimport path from 'node:path';\nimport {fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';\nimport {parseStoryboard} from './gen-shots.mjs';\nimport {SHOTS, DURATION} from './shots.js';\nimport {openChrome} from '../../會呼吸的痛/開場樣圖/v2/chrome.mjs';\n\nconst here = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));\nconst SUBTITLE_TOP = 950;\n\ntest('shots.js 与已确认的分镜一致', () => {\n  const parsed = parseStoryboard(readFileSync(path.join(here, '../storyboard.md'), 'utf8'));\n  assert.deepEqual(SHOTS, parsed);\n  assert.equal(SHOTS.length, 52);\n  assert.equal(DURATION, 333.677);\n});\n\ntest('每个定格的关键物件都在画面内，主角朝向符合分镜', async () => {\n  const chrome = await openChrome();\n  try {\n    await chrome.openStyle('paper', here);\n    const report = await chrome.evaluate('window.stage.inspectAll()');\n    const again = await chrome.evaluate('window.stage.inspectAll()');\n    assert.deepEqual(report.errors, []);\n    assert.equal(report.shots.length, 52);\n    report.shots.forEach((shot, i) => {\n      const plan = SHOTS[i];\n      assert.equal(shot.id, plan.id);\n      assert.ok(shot.keys.length > 0, `${shot.id} 没有声明关键物件`);\n      for (const key of shot.keys) {\n        const box = shot.marks[key];\n        assert.ok(box, `${shot.id} 缺少 ${key}`);\n        assert.ok(box.x1 > 0 && box.y1 > 0 && box.x0 < 1920 && box.y0 < 1080, `${shot.id} 的 ${key} 在画面外`);\n        const w = Math.min(box.x1, 1920) - Math.max(box.x0, 0), h = Math.min(box.y1, 1080) - Math.max(box.y0, 0);\n        assert.ok(w * h >= 0.6 * (box.x1 - box.x0) * (box.y1 - box.y0), `${shot.id} 的 ${key} 被裁掉过多`);\n        assert.ok(box.y0 < SUBTITLE_TOP, `${shot.id} 的 ${key} 落在字幕区`);\n      }\n      if (plan.absent) assert.equal(shot.me, null, `${shot.id} 不应出现主角`);\n      else if (plan.facing && plan.id !== 'L25') assert.equal(shot.me, plan.facing, `${shot.id} 主角朝向`);\n      assert.ok(shot.stats.spread > 12, `${shot.id} 画面过于单调：${shot.stats.spread}`);\n      assert.ok(shot.stats.meanLuma > 70, `${shot.id} 偏暗：${shot.stats.meanLuma}`);\n      assert.ok(shot.stats.purplePct < 0.5, `${shot.id} 出现紫色：${shot.stats.purplePct}`);\n      assert.equal(shot.stats.opaque, true);\n      assert.equal(shot.hash, again.shots[i].hash, `${shot.id} 两次绘制不同`);\n    });\n    assert.deepEqual(report.shots.filter(s => s.me === 'back').map(s => s.id), ['P01']);\n    assert.equal(new Set(report.shots.map(s => s.hash)).size, 52, '有重复画面');\n  } finally {\n    await chrome.close();\n  }\n});\n"
}
